issue.title: HEAD call results in ClientException: Content-Length is larger than actual response length.

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: Incorrect behavior (everything from a crash to more subtle misbehavior)

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Additional information needed from the issue author

issue.body_html:
It looks like the HTTP implementation is receiving the Content-Length and then performing its usual body-length consistency check without correctly accounting for the fact that the request was HEAD.

The HEAD call itself is fine and gives an 200 OK, but trying to do anything around a try/catch setup gets messed up by this unexpected ClientException.

comments.body_html:
1. What client are you using? Is it IOClient?
  2. I don't understand the scenario: is the server returning a content-length header but without content? Because I can't reproduce that issue if that is the case: 
      test('HEAD', () async {
    httpServerChannel.sink.add('content-length: 100\r\n');
    final response = await client.head(Uri.http(host, ''));
    expect(response.statusCode, 200);
    expect(response.headers['content-length'], '100');
    expect(response.body, '');
  });

I am sorry, I found the issue which seems to be within the fetch_client plugin, and not the native http client.
I tried reproducing it in a new Dart project and I couldn't so everything works as intended. I missed the use of this 3rd party client within the project.

Sorry for the confusion!

nodes.title: Fix #1972: bypass body-reading for HEAD requests in io_client

issue.title: Fix #1972: bypass body-reading for HEAD requests in io_client

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Additional information needed from the issue author

issue.body_html:
Fixes #1972

This PR resolves an issue where HEAD requests unexpectedly throw a ClientException due to a mismatch between the Content-Length header and the actual response body length (which is naturally empty for HEAD requests).

Because dart:io's HttpClient will sometimes fail when verifying the Content-Length of an empty HEAD response body, we now intercept HEAD requests in io_client.dart. Instead of attempting to read the body stream, we asynchronously drain the underlying connection (safely swallowing any spurious dart:io length-mismatch exceptions) and immediately return the headers with a safe, empty stream.
